clue.text: CID's possibly back in trouble with this

parts.note: the letters of CID'S are those of the word disc jumbled, so they are what a 'slipped' (rearranged) disc might give

explanation.surface: A detective from the CID admits to a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: SLIPPED is an anagram signal and DISC its fodder, which yields CIDS, so 'CID's possibly' is what the answer would build.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolapsed spinal disc is a common cause of serious back pain, so it is what puts a back in trouble.

clue.text: Condemned lifeless yoghurt in holier-than-thou fashion

indicators.note: condemned food is declared unfit, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone smugly condemns a lifeless, bacteria-free yoghurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting self-righteously means behaving with smug moral superiority, the holier-than-thou attitude.

clue.text: Entry passage given coat by paint roller

indicators.note: given coat by means the answer is covered over by the letters of the words paint roller, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A hallway is given a fresh coat by a paint roller.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece of writing, its passage of entry.

clue.text: Someone adversarial, extremely biased

parts.note: split as 'some one', some is a part and one is I, giving the letters PART and I

indicators.note: extremely means only the two end letters of adversarial

explanation.surface: An opponent in a dispute is extremely one-sided.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Someone' into 'some' (PART) and 'one' (I).
explanation.definitionFit: A partial judge or referee favours one side, so is biased.

clue.text: Driving mounted policemen around a lot

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the whole is written upwards, so read backwards
around means the police abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: the CID (Criminal Investigation Department) is the detective branch of a British police force
many means a lot

explanation.surface: Mounted police drive around a large car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted policemen' looks like police on horseback, but 'mounted' turns the whole result upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means energetic and forceful, in the sense of a driving personality.

clue.text: Somewhat contrary parrot, a timid parrot

indicators.note: contrary means the letters are taken running the opposite way
somewhat means only part of the words parrot, a timid is used

explanation.surface: A timid parrot is somewhat contrary, refusing to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The first parrot is part of the text the answer runs backwards through; the last parrot, a noun for a mimic, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot, in the figurative sense, is someone who copies others' words without thought, so a mimic.

clue.text: Sweet shade of brown hair product

parts.note: chocolate is a dark shade of brown
mousse is a foam used to style hair

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hair-dye colour, a sweet shade of brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the shade, but it is the noun meaning a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic dessert, and a sweet is the British word for a pudding course.

clue.text: Heading off, worn out, to laze around taking in unknown song from Chicago

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: frazzled means exhausted or worn out

indicators.note: taking in means the shuffled letters swallow the extra one
around means the letters of the word laze are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Someone worn out from a trip lounges about listening to a Chicago tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' drops the first letter, 'around' shuffles the lazing letters and 'taking in' adds the unknown inside them. Chicago here is the stage musical, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: This number is a showstopper from the Kander and Ebb musical Chicago, sung by the lawyer Billy Flynn.

clue.text: Do become confused, following female nonsense

indicators.note: following means the muddling word comes after the female abbreviation

parts.note: to do someone is slang for to cheat them, as is to fiddle
to addle is to become muddled or confused

explanation.surface: Someone gets muddled at a party, chasing a woman, all nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party or a mere auxiliary verb, but it is slang for cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle-faddle is an old-fashioned word for trivial talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Large 'astral' cast might be …

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A grand, star-studded cast is what an 'astral' line-up would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a cast of stars is all-star, and casting L plus ASTRAL gives the answer. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is a line-up made entirely of famous performers, which a large 'astral' (starry) cast would be.

clue.text: … backing Scot, singer briefly appearing in African capital

indicators.note: backing means the name is written going backwards

parts.note: Ian is a stereotypically Scottish first name, standing in for a Scot

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a robin is a songbird, so a singer

explanation.surface: A Scottish backing singer turns up for a gig in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like the music-industry sense to go with 'singer', but it turns IAN into NAI. The singer is a bird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Element symbolised by O, oddly

parts.note: O stands for zero; the odd letters of zero are Z and R, and Zr is the chemical symbol of this element

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which element has the symbol O, which is of course oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue wants you to say oxygen, whose symbol is O. Instead read O as zero; its first and third letters give Zr, the element's real symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a metallic element with atomic number 40, whose chemical symbol is Zr.

clue.text: Duck eaten by greedy duck

indicators.note: eaten by means the first piece goes into the mouth of the second

parts.note: avid means eager or greedy
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, drawn as an O

explanation.surface: A duck is gobbled up by a greedier duck at the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used twice with different jobs: the first Duck is a zero (O, from cricket) and the last duck is the verb meaning to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or sidestep it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Contents of clutch bag finally found in, say, front of skip

indicators.note: found in means the letter is set inside the other pieces

parts.note: eg (for example) is the abbreviation of 'say'

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of the word skip is used
finally means only the closing letter of the word bag is used

explanation.surface: Someone empties a clutch bag found tucked in at the front of a skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch bag' looks like one item, a small handbag, but the clutch belongs to the definition and the bag gives its last letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a set of eggs laid by a bird at one time, so eggs are what it holds.

clue.text: Voters potentially have online reader worried

parts.note: E (electronic) is short for online, as in e-mail
a lector is a reader, especially one who reads lessons in church
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Voters may well be anxious about a reader who posts online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' looks like an anagram signal but is ATE, the past of 'eat' in its sense of troubling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote, so potential voters collectively.

clue.text: Sort of light source OK in the pink?

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol, a source of light
well means fine or OK, as in 'all is well'

explanation.surface: A lamp is fine as a light source, if a little rosy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare named after its inventor, Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the pink is an idiom for being in excellent health, which is feeling great.

clue.text: One might tear along this …

parts.note: forms and coupons have a perforated row of dots to tear along; and the ellipsis printed after the words is itself a row of dots

explanation.surface: An instruction about tearing a page neatly, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis at the end is itself a row of dots, so the clue's punctuation points at the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated or printed row of dots marks where a coupon or slip is to be torn off.

clue.text: See 7
Fool has broken child's toy in half? Be forgiving

indicators.note: has broken means the fool splits the toy apart and sits inside it
in half means the toy is split into two halves, with the fool between them

parts.note: Lego is the plastic building-brick toy
a tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish child has broken a toy in two; a parent is urged to forgive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' uses a British slang word, and 'has broken' with 'in half' splits the toy brand around it; the question mark flags the playful use of 'broken'.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go is an idiom meaning to stop holding a grudge over it, so to forgive.

clue.text: Opera covering polar opposites? Wisdom was famously one of them

definitions.text: Wisdom was famously one of them

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means the opera sits on top of the pole letters

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini
N and S, north and south, are opposite poles

explanation.surface: An opera about polar opposites, with a famous comedian in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a much-loved British slapstick film comedian of the 1950s and 60s; 'Wisdom' is his surname, not the quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Wisdom bore that first name, so he was one of the people called Norman.

clue.text: … bank enthusiastically — eventually fishing, initially for carp

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: An angler sits enthusiastically on the river bank, eventually fishing for carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the angler's fish, but it is the verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to grumble or complain, the same sense as to carp.

clue.text: See 8
Apart from 50% of OAPs, too lazy to go round foreign capital

indicators.note: to go round means the remaining letters are spun into a new order
apart from means the two letters are left out of the words too lazy
50% of means half the word OAPs, its opening pair of letters

parts.note: OAPs are old-age pensioners

explanation.surface: Pensioners too lazy to travel round foreign capitals stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O and A (half of OAPs) from TOO LAZY, leaving TOLZY, which 'to go round' rearranges. 'Capital' means money here, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The zloty is the currency of Poland, so it is foreign money, capital in its financial sense.

clue.text: Informed about hard right, she changed point of entry

indicators.note: about means the word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: told means informed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the word she are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told about a hard-right turn says she has changed her stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the pronoun, and 'about' wraps the word for informed around everything else. 'Hard right' reads as politics but is two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the place where one steps in.

clue.text: Painting on plaster that's dry and firm

parts.note: sec is French for dry, as used of wine
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A painter's plaster has dried firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco is the technique of painting on plaster that has already dried, unlike fresco on wet plaster.

clue.text: Most attractive female consumed by sexual desire

indicators.note: consumed by means the first piece is swallowed inside the second

parts.note: lust is sexual desire
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: The most attractive woman is consumed by desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush is slang for very attractive or gorgeous, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Charge American a pound, placed on account

indicators.note: placed on means the later pieces sit after the account abbreviation

parts.note: L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An American is charged a pound, put on their account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee to go with the pound and account, but it is the noun meaning an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a formal charge against someone.

clue.text: Chicken satay and tikka starters at lunchtime, current in the western US

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does chicken

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of satay and tikka

parts.note: one o'clock is a typical lunchtime

explanation.surface: A menu of chicken satay and tikka starters served at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the meat in the satay, but it means cowardly. 'Current' is a river, not 'up to date'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellowstone River flows through Wyoming and Montana in the western United States.
